s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent pustular eruptions on the face with exacerbation by sunlight exposure
salient_findings: Mild associated pruritus without burning sensation
Exacerbation by sunlight exposure, especially in summer months
Resolution within 3-4 days, leaving mild background erythema by 5-7 days
key_facts: 4-year history of recurrent pustular eruptions on the face
Initial occurrence during a Florida vacation
Eruptions characterized by mild pruritus and intermittent occurrence
Pustules are 1-2mm and monomorphous
Located on medial cheeks, chin, and nose
No joint pain, fever, fatigue, or changes in urine color
No significant medical history
Failed response to broad-spectrum sunscreens, topical/oral antibiotics, and topical ivermectin
Serum antinuclear antibodies are negative
Anti-SSA/Ro and anti-SSB/La antibodies are negative
Bacterial swab from malar lesions is negative for growth
Histopathology shows intrafollicular and subcorneal pustule formation
